scope: Corollary 1.2 (Positive-probability transience and the velocity hemisphere) of the manuscript “Directional transience implies ballisticity” (preprints/Directional-transience-implies-ballisticity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 220 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8b305d1fbb11b2a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let d ≥ 3 and let P = ν⊗Zd be an iid law of nearest-neighbor transition rows satisfying uniform ellipticity. For a fixed ℓ ∈ Rd\{0}, set Aℓ = {Xn·ℓ −→ +∞}. If P0(Aℓ) > 0, then there is a deterministic nonzero vector v = v(ν) such that v · ℓ > 0, P0  lim n→∞ Xn n = v  = 1. If such a direction exists, then the deterministic sets of directions satisfy {u ∈ Sd−1 : P0(Au) = 1} = {u ∈ Sd−1 : P0(Au) > 0} = {u ∈ Sd−1 : v · u > 0}. In particular, P0(Au) = 0 for each fixed u ∈ Sd−1 with v · u ≤ 0, including every equator direction. The equality concerns annealed probabilities for each fixed deterministic direction, not a simultaneous pathwise assertion over all directions.
